definitions.gloss: indirectly; in a roundabout way; obliquely
definitions.explanation: Expressing something without stating it directly, often to avoid being blunt or confrontational. A very common communication style in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {遠回|とおまわ}しに⟦{断|ことわ}った→断る：02102_kotowaru⟧。
⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{遠回|とおまわ}しに⟦{不満|ふまん}→不満：02497_fuman⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伝|つた}えた→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: She expressed her dissatisfaction in a roundabout way.

examples.japanese: {遠回|とおまわ}しに⟦{言|い}わないで→言う：00515_iu⟧、⟦はっきり→はっきり：01228_hakkiri⟧⟦{言|い}って→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Don't beat around the bush — please say it clearly.

notes: Reflects a characteristic aspect of Japanese communication where directness is often avoided to maintain harmony. Common collocations include {遠回|とおまわ}しに⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧ (to say indirectly), {遠回|とおまわ}しに⟦{断|ことわ}る→断る：02102_kotowaru⟧ (to refuse indirectly), and ⟦{遠回|とおまわ}し→遠回し：08054_toomawashi⟧な⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧ (indirect expression). The な-adjective form ⟦{遠回|とおまわ}し→遠回し：08054_toomawashi⟧な is also used. The opposite approach is expressed with ⟦はっきり→はっきり：01228_hakkiri⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧ (to say clearly/directly) or ⟦{直接的|ちょくせつてき}→直接的：06093_chokusetsuteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧ (to say directly).
